pages.text: Morning sun warms the savanna. Ellie the elephant stomps gently, feeling the ground rumble under her giant feet.
She curls her long trunk to sniff the air. The trunk smells water, trees, and even tiny flowers far away.
At the river, Ellie drinks like a straw. Her trunk sucks water up, then pours it neatly into her mouth.
Ellie plucks leafy branches with her trunk and munches slowly. Elephants are plant-eaters, so greens are their fuel.
Aunties and cousins arrive. Ellie’s herd stays close, helping babies, sharing paths, and watching for trouble together.
Heat rises at noon, so Ellie heads to a muddy puddle. Cool mud feels squishy and makes her giggle.
She sprays mud on her back with her trunk. Mud can block sun and chase away itchy bugs.
After drying, the mud becomes dusty armor. Ellie scratches on a tree, then flaps her big ears to cool off.
Before sunset, the herd walks toward new grass. Ellie remembers the map: follow water, follow shade, stay together.
Night stars appear. Ellie rests beside her family, trunk tucked in, dreaming of green leaves and fresh river sips.
